checks: Verified b0296f8a3b0d3d48 at its recorded digest. Section 1 equations (1)–(2) give the contact and label conventions, and §3 equation (6) gives exactly the product, weights, and obstruction.

The lattice-preserving shear is a translation in each continuous fiber and preserves the Euclidean tangent measure on the flattened face. The homogeneous chart gives z'=z/L and the original label equation becomes Z=z(τ−a·X−b·Z). Differentiation and the rank-one determinant identity give the ordinary Jacobian L^(−n−d−1).

For the stated product, t=0 is a supporting plane shared by all sampled fibers and the apex is in the interior of each rectangular fiber at height one. Independently evaluated the chart denominators 1/2,1,3/2 and the masses 4,1,4/9 by exact rational arithmetic. In the central fiber the centroid makes the first derivative of the convex ordinary projective volume objective vanish, so a=0 is optimal there. The example only needs positivity of the base extension.

Every compact convex lift has the midpoint inclusion of its two endpoint fibers into its central fiber. Brunn–Minkowski for positive r-volumes forces the displayed rth-root inequality after the common factor cancels. The second derivative of (1+z/2)^(−2/r) is (2/r)(2/r+1)(1+z/2)^(−2/r−2)/4>0. Independently, the endpoint masses have product 16/9, so the arithmetic mean of their rth roots is at least (4/3)^(1/r)>1.

Exact evaluation of z/L gives −2,0,2/3 for the three sampled images. Since the denominator is independent of continuous coordinates, tangent lengths and perpendicular heights both scale by 1/L, yielding 2,1,2/3. The middle image label 0 differs from the endpoint midpoint −2/3.

overlap.comparison: Supplies ordinary volume distortion for centroid-normalized projective charts and covers the central-fiber optimization as a special case. It makes no assertion about exact weight representation by compatible fibers at unchanged lattice labels.

Records a Brunn–Minkowski constraint for common-scale limits of parallel Euclidean slices. The three-label weighted construction and its simultaneous violation in every positive dimension are absent there.
Gives a projective-shadow depth obstruction for a different convex example and pushforward law. It does not address uniform fiber volumes on the old labels.

readability: Minor wording suggestion: write 'the images of the three sampled bases are' before −2,0,2/3. The real base projection of the ordinary image is the interval [−2,2/3]. The surrounding argument already makes clear which three fibers are being compared.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The product gives the stated three masses and defeats any same-label uniform-volume lift in finite positive dimension, with or without common rescaling.
